$$
X=[\begin{aligned}7 & 8 & 0 & -3 \\ -2 & 10 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the sample mean vector of $X.$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the sample mean vector of $X.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the sample mean vector is given by

$$
\mathbf{m} = \dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{x}_i,
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{x}_n$ are the individual observations (columns of $X$).

From the matrix, we have that  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14198326/assets/0f27b95e2906c32bdd1cd778e65e0f3f135ef002dcec023dd3638f7d59409ec0.svg)

Therefore, the sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{4}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+{x}_{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
